item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract and is the patch I would rather review, though it still needs revision before merge.","reasons":["B adds exactly the requested Upload signature and directly reuses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", preserving the established multipart implementation.","B’s retry test uses an os.File source and verifies the complete multipart payload on both attempts, directly covering the reported streamed-content retry scenario.","B keeps the change localized to FilesService and its tests. A adds a forbidden exported association-fields option, extends multipart machinery, changes RawClient retry/body-ownership semantics globally, and edits unrelated documentation.","A explicitly violates the requirement not to add association fields or refactor retry machinery, and its Upload bypasses Add by duplicating request construction, decoding, and error handling through Raw.Do directly authorityfully? Actually no. B also bypasses public Add, but at least centralizes Add and Upload in one private implementation."],"risks_a":["Upload calls Raw.Do instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating Add’s option handling and response behavior.","WithFilesFormFields and NewFileWithFields are out-of-contract API and machinery; association fields were explicitly forbidden.","enableBodyReplay changes behavior for every raw request, including caller ownership and closing semantics, far beyond the requested scope; its shared mutable seeker also creates fragile replay semantics possibly around redirects/concurrent body access? Keep concrete visible: same seeker returned each GetBody call and no independent readers, making behavior fragile outside strictly sequential retries. Good enough maybe risk inference based code. Also failed SeekEnd may alter offset without restoring it. Need succinct. Another risk: no source reader test."],"risks_b":["Add no longer preserves existing behavior: it eagerly buffers every caller-built body, changes memory and read-error timing, and no longer passes an io.ReadCloser through to normal transport closing.","Upload does not literally route through the existing Add method; both call a new private add helper instead.","The new tests omit required validation and source-reader error cases, despite the implementation having those paths."]}
